**The data can't tell the treating team which organism caused the sepsis.** Nothing in the report supports naming a pathogen at species level.

**Top 3 non-human species by clade reads** (out of 500,000 read pairs):

| Species | Clade reads | Genus in contaminant list? |
|---|---|---|
| Cutibacterium acnes | 524 | No* |
| Acidovorax sp. JMULE5 | 331 | **Yes** (acidovorax) |
| Staphylococcus epidermidis | 182 | No |

\*Cutibacterium used to be called *Propionibacterium*, and *propionibacterium* is on the list. The literal genus name isn't, so I haven't flagged it.

**Why I can't name a cause:**
- **These are typical contaminants.** All three top species are skin flora or reagent contaminants, and each is about 0.1% of reads or less. Most of the next species are too: *E. coli* (154), *Methylorubrum* (88), *Ralstonia pickettii* (57), *Corynebacterium* (36), *Brevundimonas* (23) and *Sphingobium* (16). Five of them belong to genera on the contaminant list. "Equine infectious anemia virus" (132) is almost certainly an artefact rather than a real infection.
